$comment: Reviewed RustSec exceptions for the Buildmesh Rust dependency tree (issue #1541).
`cargo audit` treats unmaintained/unsound/yanked advisories as warnings rather than
vulnerabilities, and this repository's policy is that a warning must be either fixed or
reviewed here. Every entry carries an owner, a rationale, and a `reviewBy` date; the
`check-rust-advisories.mjs` gate fails an entry whose review date has passed, so an
exception cannot become permanent by neglect.
A `vulnerabilities` advisory (a real vulnerability, not a maintenance warning) is never
listed here: those must be fixed, which is why rustls RUSTSEC-2026-0285 was resolved in
the same change that introduced this file.

advisories.rationale: libgit2 Remote::list() can trigger undefined behaviour. The vulnerable path is libgit2's remote-list API, which Buildmesh does not call: it uses git2 for local repository, worktree and status operations only, and has no remote-fetch surface. Tracked for the next git2/libgit2 release that fixes it.

Signature created from a buffer-created BlameHunk has undefined behaviour. Buildmesh reads blame output for display only and never constructs a Signature from a BlameHunk, so the unsound path is unreachable from application code.

Unsound Iterator/DoubleEndedIterator impls in glib::VariantStrIter. glib is pulled in transitively by the GTK3 stack Tauri links on Linux; Buildmesh does not call VariantStrIter, and the crate cannot be upgraded without a Tauri GTK4 migration.

The `serial` crate is unmaintained but is a test-serialisation helper used transitively by portable-pty's own tests, not by Buildmesh code. It is a build-time-only dependency of the PTY layer with no attacker-controlled input.

yaml-rust is unmaintained and is pulled in by syntect, which Buildmesh uses for syntax highlighting of diffs and transcripts. It parses theme files that ship inside the repository, not user-supplied YAML, and syntect has no unmaintained replacement with a maintained API surface.

bincode 1.x is unmaintained. It is reached transitively through Tauri and tauri-plugin-updater. The app's own persisted state uses SQLite and JSON, not bincode, so the unmaintained crate is not on a path this repository controls; a major-version bump belongs to the Tauri upgrade.
proc-macro-error is unmaintained and is a build-time-only macro helper in the transitive graph. It cannot affect a shipped artifact's run-time behaviour.
Part of the unmaintained `unic-*` 0.9 family reached through a transitive dependency's proc-macro chain. These crates compile to Unicode tables at build time and have no run-time attack surface.
Part of the unmaintained `unic-*` 0.9 family; see RUSTSEC-2025-0081. Build-time table generation, no run-time attack surface.

yanked.rationale: libssh2-sys 0.3.2 was yanked upstream. It is vendored-by-crate into the build by libgit2-sys and is only linked for git operations; the yanked version has no known security advisory, only an upstream build-stability concern. Recorded so the warning is reviewed rather than ignored by default.
